title: Tech Note: Reading XML Made Easy with the XmlTreeWalker
author: David Adams

historical_commentary.text: This note explains the XmlTreeWalker callback-based traversal pattern built on top of 4D's classic DOM XML commands and the companion XML Tools component, aimed at developers who found manual recursive DOM tree navigation intimidating. The callback-per-node design pattern it teaches is still a conceptually sound way to flatten tree traversal, but the specific XML Tools component and its 4D 2004-era procedural language APIs have long been superseded by 4D's built-in, more capable native XML/DOM commands and by modern JSON-first data interchange, which reduced reliance on hand-rolled XML tooling. It predates 4D v11's SQL engine, Project Mode, and ORDA entirely.
related_updates: 4D's native XML/DOM command set has been extended and refined in many releases since 2007
JSON has largely replaced XML as the default data-interchange format in modern 4D development
The standalone XML Tools component approach is not part of any current, actively distributed 4D toolkit
